explanation: Read in this direction the edge says the intervention was the answer to the war. The article's first sentence: "On 19 March 2011, a NATO-led coalition began a military intervention into the ongoing Libyan Civil War to implement United Nations Security Council Resolution 1973", a resolution passed "with the stated intent to have 'an immediate ceasefire in Libya, including an end to the current attacks against civilians, which it said might constitute crimes against humanity'". The war is what was reacted to and the resolution is the form the reaction took; the coalition had no quarrel with Libya before the attacks on civilians the resolution names. Probable: Wikipedia alone.

dispute.text: The edge’s own cited article contradicts its direction, and A13 (22 September) says such an edge is marked and never silently turned round. "2011 military intervention in Libya", at revision 1370780938, opens: "On 19 March 2011, a NATO-led coalition began a military intervention into the ongoing Libyan Civil War to implement United Nations Security Council Resolution 1973 (UNSCR 1973)." That makes the intervention the answer to the war; this record says the war reacted to the intervention, which is the reverse. Turning it round is a reviewer’s act on review.html, because the two records also carry the parts of the war on either side of March 2011 and which of them the edge should run between is an editorial judgement and not a reading.
